items.title: Knicks Notes: Towns, Rosas, Coaching Staff, More
items.content:
James L. Edwards III of The Athletic is confident that the Knicks‘ front office will offer Karl-Anthony Towns an extension this offseason, but he doesn’t expect New York to put a maximum-salary contract on the table for the big man. A full max deal for Towns would be worth a projected $272.8MM over four seasons, beginning in 2027/28.

As Edwards outlines, Towns has done everything he reasonably could to prove worthy of a max contract since being acquired from Minnesota ahead of the 2024/25 season. He has been an All-Star in each of his two years with the Knicks, appeared in 147 of 164 possible regular season games, and averaged 22.2 points and 12.3 rebounds per contest. He was also an indispensable contributor during New York’s title run after adjusting to a new offensive role under head coach Mike Brown in ’25/26.

Still, Towns will be entering his age-31 season and the Knicks’ team salary is getting increasingly expensive, so a max deal for Towns would carry significant risk and would compromise the team’s spending flexibility moving forward, Edwards observes.

Because Towns holds a player option for 2027/28, he’ll remain extension-eligible throughout the season. If he and the Knicks don’t reach a new deal before opening night, he’d have to decline that ’27/28 option and replace it with the first year of a new deal in order to extend during the season.

We have more on the Knicks:

Gersson Rosas‘ departure from the Knicks was amicable, according to Stefan Bondy of The New York Post, who notes (via Twitter) that Rosas’ contract had expired, so it’s not like he stepped down or was let go. Rosas felt as if he needed to explore other opportunities in order to grow as an executive, Bondy explains. As Jared Schwartz of The New York Post writes (subscription required), in his role as the Knicks’ senior VP of basketball operations, Rosas frequently served as the team’s “point man” in trade negotiations and had a significant voice in the decision to acquire Towns, having worked with him in Minnesota.
Brown’s coaching staff isn’t expected to undergo any major changes ahead of the coming season, according to Schwartz, who says all of the front-of-bench assistants are expected to return, though there’s “a bit of uncertainty” about whether Jordan Brink will be back.
With the NBA’s regular season schedule announcement expected to happen next week, ESPN’s Vincent Goodwill notes that each Knicks/Sixers matchup in 2026/27 will be of great interest. Goodwill spoke to league insiders about how the two teams will match up and which one should be considered the favorite in the Eastern Conference.

items.title: NBA offseason grades: Did the Lakers pass or fail this summer? Report cards for all 15 teams in the West
items.content:
We gave you our Eastern Conference offseason report card.

So, it is time to hand out grades in the West, where no single team earned an A or F. That fact reflects how little movement of consequence occurred in the conference.

While NBA icons LeBron James and (we presume) Kawhi Leonard are headed East, LaMelo Ball and (we think) Brandon Ingram are the stars bound for the opposite direction, and neither moves the needle much for his new team. Same goes for Ja Morant, who was traded from the Memphis Grizzlies to the Portland Trail Blazers.

Morant and Ball may raise the ceilings for the Blazers and Minnesota Timberwolves, respectively, but they also lower their floors. In all likelihood, neither Portland nor Minnesota is any closer to contention than it was without doing a thing, so each of those teams earned a C, because we grade around the curve of: Did you get better?

Teams are also graded on asset management. Regardless of how we feel about the present state of a roster, did the franchise take steps this summer to build toward a better future? Here's looking at you, Los Angeles Lakers, who spent big, both in salary and draft picks, locking themselves into a team that is … still not a contender?

But before we give too much away, our Western Conference offseason report card …

(Dillon Marshall/Yahoo Sports Illustration)Dallas Mavericks2025-26: 26-56

2026-27 wins O/U: 34.5

Key additions: Santi Aldama • Zaccharie Risacher • Marcus Sasser • Morez Johnson Jr. • Sergio de Larrea

Key subtractions: Khris Middleton • D'Angelo Russell • Ryan Nembhard • Dwight Powell • Brandon Williams

The Cooper Flagg era is upon us, and it will continue apace in his second season with a presumably healthy Kyrie Irving in place of Ryan Nembhard at the point guard position — a pretty massive upgrade. That was the roster already in place — a mismatch of timelines (Flagg is 19; Irving is 34), but a combination of brilliant offensive players.

Around them, in the aftermath of the Luka Dončić trade, which was followed by the Anthony Davis trade — both made under the previous regime — new lead executive Masai Ujiri opted for incremental upgrades. Santi Aldama is one of the league's more underrated floor-spacing forwards, while Zaccharie Risacher and Marcus Sasser are former first-round picks who are worth a look working alongside brilliant playmakers.

Oh, and Morez Johnson Jr. — another top-10 pick, another winner — joins the rotation, along with his college coach, University of Michigan's Dusty May. The pair won the 2026 NCAA national title together and generates even more creativity for the roster.

Grade: BDenver Nuggets2025-26: 54-28

2026-27 wins O/U: 49.5

Key additions: Marvin Bagley III • Trevon Brazile

Key subtractions: Jonas Valančiūnas • Tim Hardaway Jr.
